name: Mauritian Dholl Puri
description: Dholl puri, split-pea-stuffed flatbread, is genuinely Mauritius's national dish and street food staple - real technique cooks it on a dry griddle, not fried, which is what distinguishes it from the Indian dal puri it evolved from; real Mauritian versions are traditionally eaten in pairs, wrapped around bean curry and rougaille.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

steps_detailed: Blend the split peas with the cumin, turmeric, and coriander into a fine, slightly grainy paste.
Mix the flour with water into a soft, elastic dough.
Roll out a ball of dough, place a spoonful of the pea filling in the center, and seal the dough around it, then roll out gently again into a thin round.
Cook on a hot, dry griddle, 1-2 minutes per side, without letting it brown too much - real dholl puri stays soft and pale, not fried.

name: Mauritian Rougaille
description: Rougaille, a tomato-based sauce with real Creole roots, is one of Mauritius's most essential everyday condiments, real technique built on a specific real combination of thyme, garlic, and chili together, distinguishing it from generic tomato sauces.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil, 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, and jalapeño, and simmer 15-18 minutes until thickened.

name: Mauritian Cari Gros Pois (Butter Bean Curry)
description: Cari gros pois, butter beans in a fragrant curry, is the real, traditional accompaniment to dholl puri, real technique building depth from real curry spices simmered with the beans.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic and curry powder in a little oil, 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and beans with a splash of water, and simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.

name: Mauritian Fish Vindaye
description: Fish vindaye is genuinely a fried-then-pickled dish, not a marinate-then-cook curry, which was the wrong technique here before - real mustard seed, not prepared mustard, is essential, and the onion stays crunchy rather than cooked soft, which is what gives vindaye its real pickle-like bite. Real technique fries the fish first, then briefly cooks a mustard seed, turmeric, and vinegar paste in the same oil before tossing the fried fish and raw onion through it.
steps_detailed: Season the fish with a pinch of salt and fry in the oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until just cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, mix the mustard seed and turmeric with the vinegar into a smooth paste, and cook briefly, 1-2 minutes, being careful not to let it burn or turn bitter.
Add the garlic and jalapeño, and cook 30 seconds more.

Remove from heat and toss the fried fish and raw sliced onion through the paste - real technique keeps the onion crunchy and uncooked, giving vindaye its real pickle-like bite, not a soft, cooked-down onion.

name: Mauritian Kheer
description: Kheer, a sweet rice pudding with almonds, real Mauritian versions are traditionally served alongside dholl puri, reflecting the island's deep Indian culinary heritage.
steps_detailed: Simmer the rice with the milk, stirring often, 25-28 minutes, until very soft and the mixture thickens.
Stir in the sugar and chopped almonds.

name: Mauritian Achard de Legumes
description: Achard de légumes, pickled vegetables in a real turmeric-mustard base, is a beloved Mauritian condiment, real versions genuinely reflecting both Indian and Creole culinary influence.
steps_detailed: Blanch the green beans and carrot 2-3 minutes, then drain well.
Toss with the turmeric, mustard, and vinegar, and let sit at least 30 minutes to lightly pickle.
